title: PARTICLE SWARM OPTIMIZATION FOR EXTREME VALUE ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL MAXIMUM FLOOD DISCHARGES

PPARTICLE SWARM OPTIMIZATION FOR EXTREME VALUE ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL MAXIMUM FLOOD DISCHARGES

ABSTRACT

A comprehensive understanding of the characteristics for the maximum discharges for each year for the rivers is very important for flood risk assessment and for designing hydraulic structures. This study looked at how to determine the parameters of a probability distribution of the very rare hydrologic events by using a 77-year Annual Maximum Series (AMS) for the Greater Zab River, a significant tributary of the Tigris River within Iraq, to derive parameter estimates by two of the most well-known extreme value distributions, the Gumbel distribution and the Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) distribution. Parametric estimations were formed using both Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and the performance of the models were assessed using graphs for each of the model outputs in combination with the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and the Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) data for each of the model outputs. For the benchmark assessment, the Gumbel distribution under MLE provided a better overall fit (RMSE = 53.66, KS = 0.067) than the GEV distribution (RMSE = 87.49, KS = 0.130). On the other hand, significant reductions in the RMSE of the Gumbel distribution (9.43% reduction) and the GEV distribution (58.41% reduction) were achieved when estimating the parameters of each distribution through PSO. The parameter estimates for the GEV distribution were substantially improved (RMSE = 36.39), and the shape parameter (ξ) changed from a heavy-tailed (ξ = 0.060) to a bounded-tail (ξ = -0.108), resulting in a better representation of the extreme discharge characteristics. The enhanced parameter estimates were also validated via return levels, where the 100-year discharge decreased from approximately 2341.95 m³/s (using MLE) to 2182.73 m³/s (using PSO),thus illustrating that the estimation technique used to determine the parameters of the distribution results in reduced design flood value. The results of this study show that particle swarm optimization (PSO) offers greater strength and flexibility as a method for estimating parameters and therefore can be used to improve the accuracy of hydrologic models and the reliability to predict extreme weather events when paired with optimization methods and extreme value probability distributions. The results confirm that the PSO is a better and more flexible framework for estimating parameters in comparison to conventional procedures. By using optimization techniques in combination with extreme value distribution, the accuracy of hydrologic models is increased and the reliability of the predicted values of extreme events is improved.
